newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Stada unveils plans to list shares.
newsitem.headline: German Stada unveils plans to list shares.

text.p: German generic drugs manufacturer Stada AG on Wednesday announced plans to list its shares on the bourse this fall, becoming the first German pharmaceutical group to seek a bourse listing this year.

Stada, which is based in the Frankfurt suburb of Bad Vilbel, expects to offer 17.2 million marks in new shares in October or November, raising the group's current capital of 50.2 million marks by about one third. About 350,000 new shares are expected to be issued.
The capital increase is expected to generate some 100 million marks in fresh cash which Stada has already earmarked for acquisitions.
Stada's management board chairman Hartmut Retzlaff told a news conference that the group was on the verge of snapping up a smaller competitor and entering an alliance with a research institute.

The group's share placement follows on the heels of a bourse listing for Fresenius Medical Care in 1996 and Schwarz Pharma AG and Merck KGaA in 1995 and is seen to beef up the limited supply of listed German drugs companies.
Many very profitable and sizeable drug makers, like Boehringer Ingelheim, have said they would prefer to remain private.
Trinkaus & Burkhardt, the bank handling the placement, said more details about the listing would be announced at Stada's annual meeting on June 25.

Generic drugs are drugs whose patent protection has lapsed and the market is considered to be extremely lucrative, particularly as German health care reforms are forcing physicians to prescribe cheaper variations of certain drugs.

After reporting total turnover of 343 million marks and a net profit of 13.5 million marks for 1996, Retzlaff forecast 1997 sales would rise to 400 million marks and that profits would grow by 10 to 15 percent.
Within the next two years, Retzlaff predicted Stada's turnover would soar to 600 million marks with new acquisitions generating some 100 million marks in turnover.
"The planned acquisitions should secure the pipeline of new drugs into the next century," Retzlaff said.
This fall, the group also plans to enter the French generic market.
Stada has already issued registered shares that are not freely transferable to pharmacists and physicians. The group plans to pay an unchanged dividend of 7.50 marks.
